exact_original_catalogue_text:
2.2   P02: Geometric restrictions on nef degeneration orders
Status: open in the stated generality. Book locator: Problem 25.16.1, printed p. 636.
Setup and scope. For a nef background θ and a Hermitian h, deﬁne

                                   log Vµ (θ + ϵh)                            log Vµ (θ + ϵh)
                a− (θ) = lim inf                   ,       a+ (θ) = lim sup                   .
                           ϵ↓0          log ϵ                         ϵ↓0          log ϵ

The question concerns existence of a common order, its integrality, and equality after pullback or
subtraction of an eﬀective divisorial current with nef residual.
Full problem statement. Which geometric conditions on a nonclosed nef background force a
common degeneration order, or an integral one? When is equality attained in the modiﬁcation and
residual order comparisons?
State of the art. Both orders lie in [0, n] and are independent of µ and h, of positive scaling, and
of smooth gauge. For closed nef backgrounds on a Kähler manifold they equal n−nd(θ). Nonclosed
examples on products of elliptic curves realize unequal orders, irrational common orders, and zero
volume with decay slower than every positive power. A modiﬁcation can strictly increase the orders;
eﬀective residual subtraction also gives a one-sided comparison. Explicit elliptic threefolds have
integral orders determined by the rank of their boundary forms.
Remaining gap. No unrestricted common-order or integrality assertion survives the examples.
Find hypotheses on geometry, torsion, or the degenerating positive representatives that force the
closed-type behavior, and characterize equality in the comparison inequalities.
Sources. Book, Proposition 25.16.1, Proposition 25.16.2, Proposition 25.16.5, Proposition 25.16.6;
Chapter 27’s elliptic boundary calculation.

unchanged_original_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n, theta a smooth real nef (1,1) background, h a smooth positive Hermitian form and mu a smooth strictly positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Nef means that for every epsilon>0 a smooth potential gives theta+epsilon h+dd^c u>0. For a smooth background A with a positive smooth potential representative define D_mu(gamma)=integral_X (mu/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n and lambda_mu(A)=inf_gamma integral_X A wedge gamma^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma), where gamma is any smooth positive Gauduchon metric, dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0. Put V_mu(A)=lambda_mu(A)^n; in dimension one lambda is integral A. Define a_minus(theta)=liminf_{epsilon down0} log V_mu(theta+epsilon h)/log epsilon and a_plus using limsup.
Question: find geometric hypotheses on genuinely nonclosed nef backgrounds forcing a common degeneration order, or forcing it to be integral, and characterize equality in the modification and effective-divisorial-residual comparisons in an explicit meaningful nonclosed class. A complete sufficient-condition theorem with all geometry specified is sought; an unrestricted integer-order claim is false.
Known background: 0<=a_minus<=a_plus<=n; both are independent of mu,h, smooth dd^c gauge, and positive scale. For closed nef classes on a compact Kahler manifold they equal n minus numerical dimension. Nonclosed elliptic-product examples have unequal orders, irrational common orders, or zero volume with decay slower than every positive power. The scalar Hopf threefold's single horizontal background already has order one despite failure of bounded mass. Explicit elliptic threefold boundary ranks also give known integer examples. Merely repeating these cases does not find new conditions.
For a modification pi:Y->X of smooth compact n-folds, the known comparison is a_minus(pi*theta)>=a_minus(theta) and likewise for a_plus; it can be strict for nonclosed backgrounds. For smooth nef theta,beta with a positive current (theta-beta)+dd^c phi>=0, both residual orders are at least those of theta. Effective-divisorial removal is the special case beta=theta-eta_D for a smooth curvature representative eta_D of an effective real divisor, with [D]=eta_D+dd^c phi. The residual must remain nef. Removing a divisor from an actual boundary current is distinct from the perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities, which vanish for nef backgrounds.
Find new proved hypotheses giving a common/integer order and a complete equality criterion within a fully specified nonclosed geometric family for both comparisons. Verify the exact volume or quantitative two-sided asymptotics from the full Gauduchon infimum; a formal determinant calculation without proving its variational relevance does not suffice. Keep the metric/background cone fixed and separate restricted criteria from arbitrary nonclosed classification. No candidate family or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_task.completionCriteria: Establish a complete explicit sufficient-condition result beyond the listed known isolated examples, including genuinely nonclosed backgrounds, arbitrary smooth positive mu and h, and rigorous common-order/integrality conclusions. Within the stated family prove precise equality criteria for modifications and effective-divisorial residuals, with all smooth-nef hypotheses checked. Prove every exact volume formula or needed comparison estimate from its full variational definition, check external mathematical premises at primary sources, and independently reconstruct the proof. A theorem just for closed Kahler backgrounds, a universal integrality assertion contradicted by the known examples, or a determinant of a convenient representative without a full all-test argument does not suffice. The broader arbitrary-background classification remains outside a restricted sufficient-condition theorem.

exact_primary_application_assessment: Demailly primary III.2.15 and V.13.2-13.3 were actually reread (text lines7740-7805 and14895-14932). The PDF is byte-identical to the historical native primary. Dividing its squared-norm formula by2pi gives exactly the operator and curvature sign. All sections are nonzero on the connected product or modification; singular total transforms, multiplicities and finite nonnegative real sums are in scope. Explicit section logarithms justify modification pullback; no arbitrary L1-current pullback is assumed. The optional closed-nef order theorem is supplied in the original task, not new external evidence.
mathematical_application_assessment: The all-test AMGM lower bound and the actual closed positive test prove variational relevance of the constant-rank determinant. The incidence geometry, exceptional divisor, fixed positive coefficient minima, q-section degree argument, cone-preserving residual parameters and each blockwise rank loss are checked. The optional arbitrary-Kahler-source extension claims order equality only; the product modification class also has two-sided power bounds.

clause_assessment.requested: Geometric conditions forcing common/integer orders for genuinely nonclosed backgrounds
clause_assessment.proved: A fixed positive-function cone on products of projective spaces and linear blowups has V_mu(theta+epsilon h) comparable to epsilon^(n-R(theta)), for every original mu,h. Fiber-dependent coefficients give dtheta nonzero.

Every allowed product linear blowup preserves effective block ranks and both orders. Every modification with compact Kahler source also preserves the orders after the proved all-test reduction to the task-given closed-nef fact.

For the fixed standard-metric effective divisor cone and explicit nef residual parameter conditions, equality holds exactly when every initially H-active block retains H and every initially Q-only block retains Q. All losses are blockwise nonnegative.

clause_assessment.requested: Check actual nef residual and variational definition
clause_assessment.proved: Every stated background and residual is smooth semipositive; every positive perturbation is itself positive. Distributional Gauduchon pairing, all-test AMGM and an admissible closed test establish the full original infimum, without restricting its test cone.

clause_assessment.requested: Nontrivial examples and actual divisorial removal
clause_assessment.proved: theta_t=tH+gQ has order0; removal of sE has equality exactly for s<t and an order jump ell+1 at s=t. All jumps1 through m-1 occur. The current s[E]+beta_s is explicit and is distinguished from zero minimal perturbative multiplicities.

scope_assessment: The original explicitly asks for geometric hypotheses and equality criteria. The stated nonclosed family supplies all three requested results with complete proofs. An unrestricted background/modification/residual classification was excluded by the unchanged completion criteria. This is an explicit completion-accounting correction, not an expansion of the theorem.
